highlights.title: What OpenAI’s latest controversy tells us about the future of math
highlights.summary: OpenAI’s latest mathematical milestone has quickly become mired in controversy. Today, the company announced that its agents have solved one of the Millennium Prize Problems, some of the most important open problems in mathematics.
body: It remains uncertain if OpenAI’s models made use of the work completed by Buckmaster and Alpöge, though Sébastien Bubeck, a member of the technical staff at OpenAI, said in a press briefing that the team was inspired to pursue the problem after hearing a rumor about Buckmaster and Alpöge’s efforts. But whether or not OpenAI’s models took advantage of Buckmaster and Alpöge’s research, this episode may mark a turning point in the history of mathematics.

AI models now seem essential for making progress on the most important mathematical problems of our time, and solving them may demand resources only available at a couple of frontier AI companies, which often defy the norms of academic collaboration that undergird most mathematical progress. If that’s the future we are headed for, it is unclear how human mathematicians will fit into it.

The problem that OpenAI claims to have solved is known as the Navier–Stokes existence and smoothness problem. It is one of seven Millennium Prize Problems selected by the Clay Mathematics Institute in 2000. Solutions come with a one million dollar prize; before today, only one other Millennium Prize Problem had been solved.

highlights.title: Shelton beats Alcaraz at 3.33am in New York epic
highlights.summary: Ben Shelton clinched the biggest win of his career as he defeated defending champion Carlos Alcaraz in a five-set epic stretching deep into the New York night to reach the semi-finals of the US Open.
body: The American prevailed 6-7 (5-7) 6-1 6-1 1-6 7-6 (10-7) over four hours and 28 minutes to reward a raucous Arthur Ashe Stadium crowd gripped until 3.33am in what was the latest-ever finish to a US Open match.
It marked Shelton's first career win over a top-three player, against which he had been 0-17 coming into the match.
Shelton will now play Frances Tiafoe in the final four after his fellow countryman's thrilling five-set victory over Alex Michelsen earlier in the evening.

"For me it's always about the people in the crowd, whether it's my coaches, team or friends and family, or the city of New York that showed up tonight until 3am with the USA chants, that's what kept me going and what got me this win," Shelton said on-court.

highlights.title: 'Battlestar Galactica' Meets 'Hunger Games' in 100-Episode Action Thriller That's Free on Streaming
highlights.summary: Battlestar Galactica and The Hunger Games thrive on a similar kind of pressure. Both trap remnants of human civilization within unforgiving systems with brutally high stakes where one slip-up means certain death.
body: That same volatile combination powers The 100, The CW’s post-apocalyptic action series that premiered in 2014 and ran for exactly 100 episodes. All 100 of those episodes are currently free to stream on Pluto TV.

Set 97 years after a nuclear catastrophe rendered Earth uninhabitable, the series follows the descendants of humanity’s survivors aboard the Ark, an orbital space station with a rapidly failing life-support system. Their potential solution is as absurd as it is delicious: Send 100 beautiful, incarcerated teenagers to the ruins of Earth to see whether radiation burns them alive from the inside out.

The titular 100 are a motley assortment of petty criminals, violent offenders, and Clarke Griffin (Eliza Taylor), a political prisoner locked up after discovering that the Ark is running out of oxygen. There’s also Octavia Blake (Marie Avgeropoulos), who was imprisoned for the unforgivable offense of being born (people can’t have more than one child). Once the 100 reach the ground, however, they discover a fresh start in a beautiful, dangerous world where nobody is coming to enforce the rules — and humanity may not be quite as extinct as they were told.

Both trap remnants of human civilization within unforgiving systems with brutally high stakes where one slip-up means certain death.

highlights.summary: Filmmakers describe the gig as a "hugely emotional" experience that took Noel Gallagher by surprise.
body: The search is on for a lone and emotional Oasis fan featured in a film charting the brothers' comeback tour after the first gig in Cardiff, the directors have said.
Will Lovelace and Dylan Southern's portrayal of the band's world tour in 2025 also captured the moment Liam and Noel reunited in the rehearsal studios following a 15-year hiatus.

Reflecting on the opening gig at the Principality Stadium, Southern said: "That lad in particular is amazing because he's just had the experience of his life and he doesn't know what to do with it. And we want to find him."
He went on to say: "What it resulted in and what we didn't expect is a music documentary that's actually a feel-good film."

highlights.title: Drama swirls around OpenAI’s legendary mathematical milestone
highlights.summary: OpenAI says it found a solution to a major math problem that has remained unsolved for around 90 years, as reported earlier by The New York Times and Wired. In a blog post on Tuesday, OpenAI announced that it discovered a solution to the Navier-Stokes problem - which relates to the flow of liquid…
body: OpenAI’s breakthrough with a 90-year-old problem is challenged by researchers who solved a related problem the day before.

OpenAI says it started training the internal AI model on August 28th, which has “exhibited unprecedented performance in our benchmarks, including mathematics.” The solution is a big breakthrough for the mathematics community, but it doesn’t come without controversy.

Just one day before OpenAI’s announcement, New York University mathematics professor Tristan Buckmaster published findings on a related problem in partnership with Levent Alpöge, a researcher at Anthropic. When announcing these findings, Buckmaster claims he contacted OpenAI after learning the company had heard about their progress. However, Buckmaster found that OpenAI had produced a proof for the Navier-Stokes equation using a route he and Alpöge had been working on with OpenAI’s Codex and Anthropic’s Claude.

highlights.title: F1's toughest street track ever? Why new Madring could cause Spanish GP chaos
highlights.summary: Formula 1 has a brand-new track to look forward to this weekend and the expectation is there will be carnage and the drivers will be seriously tested at the Madring.
body: The Spanish Grand Prix has moved from its traditional circuit in Barcelona to a high-speed street track in Madrid and has been described as "Jeddah on steroids" by Formula 3 drivers who tested there last month - the Jeddah track itself is one of the most challenging circuits in F1.
So why is the Madring so difficult and how will it impact the racing we see this weekend, live on Sky Sports F1?
There are 22 official corners on the 3.365-mile Madring circuit, although unusually the track layout has Turns 5A and 20A - so maybe there are 24.
Whatever the number, after the start/finish straight the driver will almost always be turning the steering wheel at some point as there are few straights.

highlights.title: Marvel Phase 7 and 8 Movie Slate and Release Dates: 'Black Panther 3,' 'Shang-Chi 2' and Beyond
highlights.summary: Like Doctor Strange himself, Marvel Studios has its eyes fixed on the future, with a carefully plotted release calendar extending well beyond the highly anticipated events of Avengers: Secret Wars, which is currently set to hit theaters in December 2027.
body: Marvel’s release calendar is always subject to change, but the studio’s plans after Secret Wars are becoming easier to read. The MCU’s next era seemingly won’t be built around the same heroes who carried the Infinity Saga, as the X-Men and Marvel’s supernatural characters appear poised to steal the limelight.

Based on Marvel’s announced projects, Kevin Feige’s comments, and the studio’s current direction, here’s what Phase 7 might look like. Keep in mind that although Marvel has booked these release dates, its two 2029 movies remain entirely speculative.

In the wake of Doomsday, Marvel’s Secret Wars will drop its heroes into one of their most harrowing situations yet. Although little has been confirmed about the movie’s plot, its title evokes two landmark comic-book crossovers. The original 1984 story brought Marvel’s heroes and villains together on a patchwork planet created by the Beyonder, while Jonathan Hickman and Esad Ribić’s 2015 series followed Doctor Doom as he ruled a new Battleworld assembled from the remains of destroyed realities.

Savvy Games Group: Brian Ward is stepping down as CEO of the Saudi-backed games conglomerate, with Turqi Alnowaiser, deputy governor of Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, taking over as interim CEO. Ward had led Savvy since 2021, overseeing a roughly $38bn investment push into the games industry that included the acquisition of Scopely and stakes in companies including Nintendo and Embracer Group.

Supercell: Lasse Seppänen has left the company after seven and a half years, most recently as GM of Supercell London, to pursue new game IP ventures, with plans to start his own studio in 2027. Separately, Luran Zhang has joined as community manager after nearly four years at Lilith Games working on Rise of Kingdoms, and Mateusz Janczewski has joined as game producer.

highlights.title: Europe’s wildest pilgrimage route: a trek through the mountains of north-west Sweden
highlights.summary: A remote 18th-century chapel deep in Sami lands is the goal of the Präststigen, a 37-mile trail that traverses some of the country’s most spectacular scenery. I wasn’t exactly in “Sunday best”, but I had made some effort.
body: I had hiked to Alkavare following the Präststigen, or “Priests’ trail”, a 37-mile (60km) route from Kvikkjokk that could stake a claim as Europe’s wildest pilgrimage route, and certainly one of its most beautiful. The Präststigen follows the path that priests would once have taken to the chapel, built in 1788, to perform a service each summer, and today, on the last weekend in July, intrepid hikers and perseverant pilgrims can attend that same service.

Alkavare sits on the western border of Sweden’s Sarek national park, home to many of the country’s highest mountains and steepest valleys, yet with no campsites or tourist huts and only scant sections of the more famous Kungsleden trail. There are no other marked paths and to hike here means wild camping, a heavy backpack and a sense of adventure. It was described by famed Swedish diplomat Dag Hammarskjöld in 1926 as vår sista stora vildmark – “ our last great wilderness”.

highlights.title: ChatGPT Sketch turns your bad drawings into detailed AI images
highlights.summary: OpenAI announced ChatGPT Images 2.5 on Tuesday and is adding a new way to tell ChatGPT what you want it to make an image of: by drawing a doodle. With a new feature called Sketch, you can just draw something right inside ChatGPT and then tell ChatGPT how you want it to make an image based on that…
body: OpenAI’s updated image generation tools in ChatGPT let you use a doodle as part of your prompt.

You can activate the Sketch feature by typing @Sketch into your chat box, and a window will pop up where you can make your drawing. I briefly tested it, and it successfully turned my bad doodle of a cat that I drew with my computer mouse into a realistic photo, per my instructions. You can also now leave comments directly on parts of images that you want changed, which I used to make the cat’s eyes green instead of blue.

As for ChatGPT Images 2.5, OpenAI says that it makes images with “more natural lighting and richer textures,” is better at following your editing instructions “across multiple turns,” and that image generation latency has been reduced by “up to 50% compared with Images 2.0.” ChatGPT Images 2.5 is out now for ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work, and Codex users on desktop, mobile, and web, according to OpenAI.

highlights.title: Trump administration to confront Australia over Labor’s social media algorithm plan
highlights.summary: White House warns trading partners against ‘imposing digital services taxes, fines, and other forms of extortion’ on US tech sector. Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates. Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast.
body: The Trump administration will confront Australia over its plan to force digital platforms to take down harmful content and let users opt out of algorithm-generated “for you” feeds.
Big tech companies would be fined more than $100m for breaching the proposed laws and the Australian government is under pressure to raise those fines even further.

A White House spokesperson, Kush Desai, said the US administration would raise its concerns with “trading partners”, in a statement released less than 24 hours after Australia’s announcement on Tuesday.
“President Trump has unequivocally warned trading partners against imposing digital services taxes, fines, and other forms of extortion on America’s leading technology sector,” Desai said.

highlights.title: From honeymoon vision to the Super Bowl - can Seahawks win it all again?
highlights.summary: Honeymoons are for newlyweds celebrating true love and for future NFL head coaches plotting Super Bowl glory. At least in the case of Mike Macdonald, who has now turned to the Chicago Bulls as his recipe reference for a repeat.
body: Mystic Macdonald went viral earlier this year when the Seattle Seahawks released footage of his first-ever team meeting upon being appointed in 2024. Within it, he had strayed from his script to forecast a place at the NFC Championship Game and an 'inevitable' feel to a 'won't die, won't quit' machine.
"It probably came to me about 30 minutes before the meeting," Macdonald tells Sky Sports of his viral speech.
Between some fine fortune-telling and a relentless winning formula, that vision became a reality 21 months later as Seattle beat the Los Angeles Rams to reach Super Bowl LX.

It would eventually culminate in Macdonald's skyward gaze towards the cloud of confetti and fireworks honouring his Seahawks as NFL champions following their victory over the New England Patriots at Levi's Stadium in February.

highlights.title: Muse, Meta’s New Personal AI Agent, Needs You to Trust It
highlights.summary: Designed to compete with OpenClaw and Instinct, the company says Muse can do everything from sell your car to book you a plane ticket.
body: Meta announced Tuesday the release of Muse, a personal AI agent that people can message to automate digital tasks in a secure cloud environment, all while relying on security and privacy that the company says is “built into it” from the start.

Meta says Muse is rolling out today for iOS and Android users in a dedicated Muse app, as well as the website Muse.ai. The company also says users can directly message Muse in WhatsApp to interact with the agent. Meta says users of its AI glasses will soon be able to interact with its Muse agent as well. Meta says people can try out Muse for free, but users who want to automate lots of digital tasks will need one of the company’s AI subscription plans.

Muse is Meta’s latest attempt to compete with viral AI agents such as OpenClaw and Instinct, which users can message with to automate digital tasks. Muse is a product of Meta Superintelligence Labs, the AI unit CEO Mark Zuckerberg formed roughly a year ago to catch up with OpenAI and Anthropic, offering some researchers eye-popping compensation packages to join. The unit was built on the belief that AI agents will transform how everyday users navigate the internet, as well as Meta’s products.

highlights.title: A moment that changed me: I spent a day with some naturists – and it cured my shy bladder
highlights.summary: For decades, I had been haunted by paruresis, an inability to urinate in public toilets. But that day of nakedness suddenly, surprisingly, led me to shed my inhibitions. For as long as I can remember, I’ve suffered from a condition called paruresis – also known as shy bladder syndrome.
body: I’m a writer, so am often out and about meeting people in cafes, hotels and at events. My agricultural background means I also meet a lot of my interviewees on farms – but at least there I could pop behind a hedge if I needed to go, and be assured of privacy.

It was while I was doing research for a book on the spiritual connections humans once had with the land that I stumbled across the Christian Naturist Fellowship: a network of people who believe that Christianity and naturism are entirely compatible. Here, I thought, were a community who clearly get closer to nature than most – I was keen to meet them.

One of their committee members, Nigel, suggested I visit his naturist club near Colchester. So one Saturday morning in 2025, I set off to discover what Christian naturists really think and do. He had said that I’d not have to strip off – many don’t on their first visit – but when the time came, that is exactly what I did.

highlights.title: Apple expected to unveil folding iPhone as new CEO takes center stage
highlights.summary: The new model will serve as the first big test for John Ternus, who took the role last week. All eyes are on Apple’s annual fall announcement of new products this afternoon, where the company is expected to unveil the most significant change to the iPhone since the smartphone’s introduction in…
body: Unlike previous iterations, the new iPhone is expected to fold, opening and closing like a passport to double its screen size.
The product release event, titled “Surprise and Shine”, begins at 10am Pacific Standard Time on Apple’s campus in Cupertino, California, south of San Francisco.

While competitors have released foldable smartphones since the late 2010s, the new model will be a first for the iPhone maker and will also serve as the first big test for the company’s new CEO, John Ternus, who assumed the role on 1 September.

Apple is expected to price the phone north of $2000, more than what some of its competitors charge for their foldable phones. A Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold, for instance, retails for $1899. Much remains unknown about Apple’s device, including its name, though it is rumored to be named either the iPhone Fold or the iPhone Ultra.

highlights.summary: Some shows change television forever. Anthologies have never been the same since The Twilight Zone, the modern sitcom owes a lot to I Love Lucy, and puzzle-box mysteries all had to step up their game after Lost.
body: Speaking of crime dramas with unforgettable legacies, Miami Vice (1984–1990) also left a massive cultural imprint. Although the NBC show did nothing novel in terms of storytelling, Miami Vice ’s use of striking pastel shades and frenetic camera work made it stand out from genre fare. If you’ve been meaning to check this groundbreaking series out, there’s good news: All five seasons of Miami Vice are now available to stream for free on Tubi.

Miami Vice follows detective sergeants James "Sonny" Crockett (Don Johnson) and Ricardo "Rico" Tubbs (Philip Michael Thomas), who team up to fight crime — and do so in style. Crockett and Tubbs are supported by a core cast and a revolving door of guest stars, including the likes of Laurence Fishburne, Viggo Mortensen, Ben Stiller, Bruce Willis, and Liam Neeson, among others. Following a case-of-the-week format, Miami Vice keeps things fairly lighthearted in the initial seasons, but turns darker and more cynical as Crockett and Tubbs explore the seedy underbelly of crime and corruption in the neon-tinted streets of Miami.

highlights.title: I climbed into the car with three friends. I woke in hospital to find I’d lost them all – and my legs
highlights.summary: Rob Pike was 17 when he and three of his closest friends were in a car that smashed into a tree and split in half. He explains how he coped with the devastation. After the car stopped rolling and came to rest on its side, Rob Pike remembers being “hyperfixated” on the rainwater pouring down his…
body: He was in the back seat next to his best friend, Daniel McCoy. “I look up to my left to see if Daniel’s OK. He’s probably about a foot away from my face and … he’s not OK. I’m looking at my dead best friend and I wish that wasn’t my last memory of him, seeing how broken he was.” They were 17.

“I lost control,” he says. “I am screaming at the top of my lungs. I’m yelling, I’m crying.” Even though he knew that Daniel was dead, he hoped for a miracle. “You spend your life watching Home and Away and Neighbours and you see people getting pulled out of cars and having CPR. If I can scream loud enough, then maybe somebody might come along and save his life.”

A woman had rushed out of her house when she heard the crash and run towards Pike’s screams. She found the car in the bushes. Pike remembers begging her: “‘Please help Daniel. You gotta do something.’ And then she gets down on her hands and knees, in the mud, in the rain, and she looks inside. And I remember her saying: ‘There’s nothing we can do for him. He’s already gone.’

highlights.title: Meta bets on AI agent Muse to catch up in AI race
highlights.summary: Meta is making another push to bring artificial intelligence to the masses with Muse, a personal assistant it says can put AI in the hands of virtually anyone. The product is the latest step in a multi-billion-dollar strategy overhaul designed to revitalize the company's ailing position in the AI…
body: Meta drills down on ease of use and privacy options after spending billions overhauling its AI strategy.

Muse is a “personal AI agent” designed to help out with everyday tasks and projects, like online shopping, sending emails, and planning a trip. Once given a goal, Meta says Muse can work on its own, opening a browser, filling out forms, and even negotiating on users’ behalf. For lengthy tasks, Meta says Muse will continue working in the background after users close the app, returning to users if something changes or if it requires approval for something, such as making a purchase.

Muse will roll out in the US on iOS, Android, and muse.ai, with AI glasses “coming soon.” The assistant will be free for most users, though Meta said there will be paid subscriptions “for people who want to do more.” The company did not specify the nature and costs of these paid plans, nor outline what limits there are for free users.
“Muse is a first step: an agent that takes on more of the work so people can focus on what matters to them,” Meta said.

highlights.title: UK datacentres will create just 25% of jobs predicted by tech sector, analysis finds
highlights.summary: Facilities likely to employ 10,400 workers, compared with 40,000 in industry estimates, thinktank says. Datacentres in the UK will create just a quarter of the jobs predicted by the tech sector, while consuming vast amounts of energy, according to new research.
body: Environmental thinktank Verdant predicts that all the datacentres currently planned are likely to directly employ 10,400 workers – compared with the more than 40,000 cited in projections by the industry lobby group TechUK.

Labour has defended the rapid rollout of AI datacentres in the face of growing public scepticism, amid concerns about their demand for water and energy. The government has also echoed TechUK’s claims about job creation.

Verdant’s analysis is based on 20 projects for which data on staffing levels are publicly available, including via planning applications, company accounts and press releases – as well as international comparisons.

It says the datacentres that have already been built have directly created fewer than 4,400 jobs – about 8.6 jobs for each megawatt of energy they consume, against the 43.7 jobs claimed in TechUK’s projections.

body: McMurtry's 1985 bestseller follows former Texas Rangers-turned-cowboys Augustus "Gus" McRae and Woodrow Call, who embark on a fateful 3000-mile cattle drive to Montana, encountering a variety of frontier dangers along the way.

CBS adapted it as a blockbuster TV miniseries in 1989 starring Robert Duvall, Tommy Lee Jones, Danny Glover, Rick Schroder, Diane Lane, Robert Urich, Anjelica Huston, Steve Buscemi, Chris Cooper, Frederic Forrest, and Glenne Headly.

“After our singular experience on East of Eden, we are thrilled to be teaming with Netflix again, along with Teton Ridge Entertainment, to bring Larry McMurtry’s western classic to life,” Kazan and Stuart said in a statement (via Deadline ).
“We come to this material with love and respect, and can’t wait to hit the trail with Gus and Call and the rest of these beloved characters. Yee-haw.”

highlights.title: Babies born to anaemic mothers have smaller brains, study finds
highlights.summary: Key regions of the brain linked to movement, learning and emotions were affected and may lead to cognitive problems. Babies born to mothers with anaemia have smaller brains, particularly in key regions linked to movement, learning and the regulation of emotion, according to a study.
body: Researchers said the differences, first detected at the age of one, could lead to cognitive problems when children started school.

More than a third of pregnant women worldwide have anaemia – a condition typically caused by iron deficiency in which the number of red blood cells in the body is lower than normal. Symptoms include fatigue, shortness of breath and dizziness. Rates are highest in sub-Saharan Africa and south Asia.

Researchers from King’s College London in the UK, and the University of Cape Town in South Africa, followed more than 300 mothers and their babies in Cape Town, scanning the brains of the infants several times between the ages of three months and two years.

On average, the total brain volume of babies born to anaemic mothers was 4% lower than that of babies born to non-anaemic mothers – despite all the anaemic mothers being diagnosed only with a mild version of the condition.

highlights.title: How GPT-5.6 Sol helps run quantum computing experiments
highlights.summary: See how an MIT researcher uses GPT-5.6 Sol with Codex to autonomously run quantum computing experiments, analyze results, and calibrate qubits.
body: Connecting GPT‑5.6 Sol to laboratory software to run and refine routine measurements on quantum chips freed Beatriz Yankelevich to focus on experiment design and data analysis.

Quantum computing is an emerging technology that uses the unique properties of quantum mechanics to process information. It could one day better simulate complex materials and molecules. Unlike conventional processors, quantum processors are built with quantum bits, or qubits. Preparing and running qubit experiments can take months and require hundreds to thousands of preliminary measurements—work that AI is poised to help with.

Beatriz Yankelevich, a graduate student in MIT’s Engineering Quantum Systems Group (EQuS), used GPT‑5.6 Sol, harnessed to Codex, to explore whether AI could streamline her experimental workflow. The MIT group studies superconducting qubits, which are cooled to near absolute zero inside specialized devices called dilution refrigerators. These qubits perform operations quickly, are precisely controlled using microwave signals, and can be made using familiar manufacturing techniques and arranged on a chip.

highlights.title: “Salomon Should Not Be a Fashion Brand”: The New Creative Director Shares His Manifesto
highlights.summary: Despite substantial growth, the footwear brand is restrategizing. Creative director Heikki Salonen and CEO Guillaume Meyzenq want to unify Salomon’s hyper-technical product offering with the lifestyle-led designs.
body: Salomon sneakers weren’t always cool. Just ask creative director Heikki Salonen, who wants to restore the very geekiness that first attracted a trendier customer set to the French outdoors label. “When I started, I was adamant about the idea that Salomon should not be a fashion brand,” says the Finnish designer, video calling from Salomon HQ in Annecy, southeastern France. “We should keep on doing what we do the best, which is performance-driven — but performance in a non-traditional way.”

Salonen joined in January as the brand’s first official creative director, following a six-year stint as the anonymous creative director of Maison Margiela’s legacy diffusion line, MM6. Before that, he’d worked as collection director — leading on clothing — from around 2013. During his time at MM6, he oversaw several collaborations with Salomon, quickly recognizing a market for fashion-forward performance shoes.
